newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shares close at record on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shares close at record on foreign buying.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange surged to new record highs in busy trading Friday as foreign investors bought into what they see as a sustained bullish trend for Venezuelan stocks, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index rose 1.79 percent to 4,949.15 as stocks rose virtually across the board.
A total of 34 stocks closed higher, four lower and four unchanged, the exchange said.
"There was demand by foreign in certain shares due to the country's improved prospects," one broker said.
Other brokers noted that foreign investors had begun to look to non blue chip stocks in search of attractive prices.

Blue chips stock prices, "already reflect the companies' value so it has become more attractive for foreigners to buy less liquid stocks which they hope will perform well over the medium term," said Boris Molina, analyst with the Merinvest brokerage.
The search for attractive prices gave the market depth and breadth in strong trading of 4,274 billion bolivars ($9 million).

Among leading stocks, benchmark Electricidad de Caracas rose 7.00 bolivars to 435.00 bolivars, steel company Sivensa rose 10.00 bolivars to 310.00 bolivars and plastic container manufacturer Envases rose 4.00 bolivars to 105.00 bolivars.

Brokers said high levels of liquidity and low interest rates at home combined with a bullish mood among foreign investors should see the market continue to rise, with occasional breaks for profit-taking, for some time.
